enterprise_workflows.flow_intro.en_value: Set up multi-step approval routes for any entity type, then track every request from submission through to a final decision.

enterprise_workflows.flow_step_1_desc.en_value: Name the workflow, choose the entity type it governs (change orders, variations, invoices, etc.) and add approval steps with the required approvers.

enterprise_workflows.flow_step_2_desc.en_value: Toggle the workflow to active so it starts receiving requests. Inactive workflows are paused without being deleted.

enterprise_workflows.flow_step_3_desc.en_value: When a record triggers an approval, it appears in the Approval Requests tab. Approve or reject each step, and the request advances or stops.

enterprise_workflows.flow_step_4_desc.en_value: Filter requests by status to see what is pending, approved or rejected. The audit trail records who decided and when.

enterprise_workflows.no_requests_desc.en_value: Approval requests will appear here when submitted.

enterprise_workflows.no_workflows_desc.en_value: Create your first workflow to set up approval processes.

enterprise_workflows.subtitle.en_value: Configure approval workflows and manage pending requests across your projects.

jobs.empty_desc.en_value: Background jobs will appear here when tasks are queued.

jobs.flow_intro.en_value: Background jobs handle heavy work off the main thread so the interface stays responsive. This page is the single place to watch, cancel and inspect every queued task.

jobs.flow_step_1_desc.en_value: Long-running operations such as PDF generation, data imports and cost recalculations are sent to the background queue instead of blocking the UI.

jobs.flow_step_2_desc.en_value: Each job shows its kind, status and a live progress bar. Click a row to see timing, the Celery task ID, result payload or error details.

jobs.flow_step_3_desc.en_value: Stuck or unnecessary jobs can be cancelled while they are pending or running. Finished jobs let you download the result or error payload as JSON.

jobs.flow_step_4_desc.en_value: Narrow the list by status or job kind, and search across the current page. Server-side pagination keeps the view responsive even with thousands of runs.

jobs.subtitle.en_value: Monitor and manage background tasks running on the server

rebar_schedule.delete_message.en_value: This will permanently remove the import and all its shapes. This cannot be undone.

rebar_schedule.drop_abs.en_value: Drag and drop an .abs file here

rebar_schedule.empty_desc.en_value: Upload an ABS file above to get started.

rebar_schedule.flow_intro.en_value: Import bar-bending schedules from ABS files, review parsed shapes and weights, and produce cutting lists grouped by diameter for procurement.

rebar_schedule.flow_step_1_desc.en_value: Drag and drop or browse for a .abs bar-bending schedule file. The parser reads bar marks, shape codes, dimensions and quantities.

rebar_schedule.flow_step_2_desc.en_value: Before committing, check the parsed shapes and any warnings. Fix problems in the source file and re-upload if needed.

rebar_schedule.flow_step_3_desc.en_value: Open an import to see every bar mark with its shape, diameter, length, quantity and unit weight. Stat cards show totals at a glance.

rebar_schedule.flow_step_4_desc.en_value: The cutting list groups bars by diameter and totals the count and weight, ready for ordering or export back to .abs.

rebar_schedule.no_project_desc.en_value: Choose a project from the header to manage its rebar schedules.

rebar_schedule.preview_subtitle.en_value: Review the parsed file before importing.

rebar_schedule.subtitle.en_value: Import, validate and manage reinforcement bar schedules from ABS files.

rfq_bidding.empty_desc.en_value: Create your first request for quotation to start collecting bids.

rfq_bidding.field_title_placeholder.en_value: e.g. Concrete supply for Block A

rfq_bidding.flow_intro.en_value: Create a request for quotation, send it to vendors, collect and compare their bids, then award the best offer - all in one place.

rfq_bidding.flow_step_1_desc.en_value: Describe the scope, set a due date and list the vendors you want to invite. The RFQ stays in draft until you are ready.

rfq_bidding.flow_step_2_desc.en_value: Issue the RFQ and vendors receive an invitation to bid. They submit pricing against each scope line before the due date.

rfq_bidding.flow_step_3_desc.en_value: Open the comparison matrix to see every vendor side by side, line by line. The lowest total is highlighted automatically.

rfq_bidding.flow_step_4_desc.en_value: Select the winning bid, and the award is recorded with the vendor, amount and date. Past awards are available for audit on the Awards tab.

rfq_bidding.no_awards_desc.en_value: Awards will appear here once you select winning bids from the comparison view.

rfq_bidding.no_bids_desc.en_value: Bids will appear here once vendors submit their quotations.

rfq_bidding.no_project_desc.en_value: Choose a project from the header to manage its RFQs.

rfq_bidding.no_rfq_selected.en_value: Select an RFQ to compare bids

rfq_bidding.no_rfq_selected_desc.en_value: Choose an RFQ from the dropdown above to see a side-by-side bid comparison.

rfq_bidding.subtitle.en_value: Manage requests for quotation, compare bids and track awards

saved_views.delete_message.en_value: This will permanently remove the saved view. Other users who shared this view will lose access.

saved_views.empty_desc.en_value: Saved views are created from the filter bar on any list page. Build a filter, click "Save view" and it will appear here.

saved_views.flow_intro.en_value: Save a filter spec against any registered entity, share it with a team or a project, and reuse it as a list, count, tile or export.

saved_views.flow_step_1_desc.en_value: Open any list in the platform (positions, contacts, submittals, etc.) and set the columns, sorting and conditions you need.

saved_views.flow_step_2_desc.en_value: Give the filter a name, choose who can see it (private, team, project or workspace) and pin it for quick access.

saved_views.flow_step_3_desc.en_value: Open a saved view to get the latest results, use its count on a dashboard tile, or export the rows to CSV.

saved_views.flow_step_4_desc.en_value: Views are validated against the current schema. A stale badge appears when a referenced field is removed or renamed so you can fix it before it breaks.

saved_views.no_project_desc.en_value: Choose a project from the header to manage its saved views.

saved_views.subtitle.en_value: Reusable filter specs you can share, pin and export.

timeline.flow_intro.en_value: A chronological feed of every meaningful event on the project, collected from all modules so you can see what happened, who did it, and when.

timeline.flow_step_1_desc.en_value: Every create, update, status change and deletion across all modules is logged automatically with a timestamp, actor and affected entity.

timeline.flow_step_2_desc.en_value: Events appear in reverse chronological order. Click any row to expand its details, including status transitions, metadata and a link to the record.

timeline.flow_step_3_desc.en_value: Narrow the feed by module, action type or date range. The search bar also matches entity types and reasons across the current page.

timeline.flow_step_4_desc.en_value: Download the current view as CSV for offline review or compliance reporting. The export includes all visible columns and respects active filters.
